subject: low coverage data, how to use for DMR analysis

messages.author: 21065eb57dfbc0bd
messages.subject: low coverage data, how to use for DMR analysis
parts:
Hi the data that I am currently analysing is a low coverage whole genome bisulfite sequencing data. I complained to my collaborator that the data is pretty low coverage (3-4x on an average) .He has been involved in analysis of such data earlier he said to use a 50bp window that way you would have a 50*3 coverage for that particular region. When I use methylkit I have to throw many positions away as they fall below depth of 10. If I take tiles (50bp) then do you think the analysis would be more viable. Also can I use eDMR for whole genome bisulfite sequencing as the paper talks about ERRBS. Please let me know. The analysis I had done so far was not strand specific so I don't know if the filtering criteria applies irrespective of the strand or for total of the two strands.

thanks

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] low coverage data, how to use for DMR analysis
parts:
you can keep bases that are below 10X coverage in methylKit, then you can tile 50 bp windows. I don't think you can use eDMR because it is designed for clustering of DMCs based on distribution of distances between nearest CpGs and may be optimized for that assumption not for tiling windows (Sheng Li may comment on this)

you can do what you suggested in general, loosen the coverage threshold and tile windows over the genome, and as you say people do it. I don't know if the methylation estimates would be reliable with 3-4X coverage. To test that, you can take a high coverage whole-genome BS or RRBS data set, down-sample the coverage (aligned reads) to  3-4X and tile 50 bp windows, also tile 50 bp windows from the original set and check the correlation/scatter plot between these two sets. If they are very different, you need to get more coverage.

Best,
Altuna

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Re: low coverage data, how to use for DMR analysis

Best,
Altuna
